prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create an original illustrated portrait of Jackie Leven around 1983 for the next chapter of a dark biographical homage website.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPHIC subject reference, a record cover with a woman on the left and Jackie Leven on the right. The MAN ON THE RIGHT is the sole subject. Use his actual face, clean-shaven appearance, age, slim facial proportions and long swept-back dark hairstyle. Completely remove the woman, typography, cover design, photographic studio setting, original seated arrangement and hand-under-chin pose.
Image 2 (Doll by Doll portrait) and image 3 (older man with guitar) are STYLE AND TONAL REFERENCES ONLY from the approved illustration series. Do not transplant their faces, ages, hairstyle, pose or instruments into this picture. The new portrait must have the likeness of the man in image 1.

LIKENESS:
Jackie in his early thirties, as in photo 1. His distinctive high forehead and hairline, long straight dark hair swept back off the forehead and falling toward and just past the shoulders, brows and watchful slightly hooded eyes, straight nose, slim cheeks, quiet closed mouth and natural jaw. Clean-shaven, no moustache or beard. Preserve the individual asymmetries and proportions of the photographed face; do not prettify him into a generic handsome rock musician or age him into the older style reference. Hair is brushed back, loose in long strands at the sides and back, not a ponytail, topknot, mullet, centre-parted curtain or contemporary haircut.

NEW COMPOSITION:
One head-and-shoulders / upper-chest portrait in a vertical 4:5 frame. Camera at eye level rather than the photo's high viewpoint. Head very gently turned toward the viewer's left, eyes looking directly toward the viewer, subtle contrary turn of the relaxed shoulders. Serious, alert, self-possessed, understated expression. Both hands out of frame; no fist against chin. Entire head and long hair visible with dark breathing room around it. Suggest the original loose open-neck shirt with just a few broken collar and chest marks, rendered in dark muted greys rather than a big white shirt. Torso, collar edges and shoulders dissolve into darkness. No props, instruments, accessories or other figures.

VISUAL LANGUAGE:
Match the approved dry-brush ink portrait series. Use a limited number of broad, matte, muted grey pigment shapes, selective directional hatching and expressive broken brush gestures. Strongly simplify hair and clothing. The face remains recognizable through accurately placed eyes, nose and mouth, but the light/shadow planes are visibly hand-drawn, interrupted and economical rather than photorealistically modelled. Rough torn stroke edges, dark unworked gaps and natural irregularity. Avoid many fine lines, hair-by-hair detail, skin pores, slick digital polish, smooth airbrushed gradients, mechanical vector posterization, ornamental engravings, glossy impasto, or artificial embossed pebbly all-over texture. Style 2 is the clearest guide to how much to abstract facial light and shadow; style 3 guides how to let the torso almost disappear.

COLOUR AND LIGHT:
Near-black anthracite #0d0f12 ground; monochrome NEUTRAL grey only. No brown, sepia, beige, cream, yellow, red or colour tint. Compressed low-key values with broad light face planes approximately #60666a to #74797c and a few small accents around #85898c, no white. Hair and shirt are mostly deep charcoal and negative space. Same subdued watermark-like presence and contrast as the style references. Natural positive facial lighting, dark pupils, nostrils and mouth inside grey face planes; never an inverted image. Slight directional light with enough local contrast to read the eyes and mouth at website size. Quiet intensity rather than theatrical drama.
Every outside edge fades organically into plain anthracite so the picture fits the website without a visible rectangular boundary. No frame, halo or paper border. No text, signature, lettering, labels, album graphics, logos, background scene or extra elements. One standalone portrait.
